headline: Reproducible pipelines and benchmarks for long- and short-read sequencing analysis
label: Sequencing Data Analysis Tools
summary: New open tools and donor-resolved benchmarks target reproducibility and error profiling across long- and short-read sequencing workflows.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reproducible, packaged software for sequencing analysis, with several items also addressing error characterization. CREPAS provides a Nextflow pipeline for nascent and parental chromatin sequencing, and SC-framework pairs a containerized Python package with guided notebooks for single-cell data. TelomereHunter2 adds containerization and reports up to 74% faster runtime. Bamsnap-LRS automates batch visualization of long-read alignments. Benchmarking nine short-read chemistries on seven sequencers with donor-specific assemblies measures true platform errors; HiFiRE3 combines error correction with artifact-aware libraries for rare structural variants. The Landrace pig gapless assembly and an open ASE pipeline extend these resources to livestock genomics. Relative to earlier items, the new emphasis is on reproducibility, containerization, and ground-truth benchmarking.
